narratives.Overview:
## Summary

AppSec scan on **`0c382e91`** (post-**#3354**) found two **HIGH** UAT Shell classification residuals.

Under active UAT, further write-capable binaries still classify empty / unclassifiable and **allow** write-shaped Shell. That path can plant a forged `.deft/authz` grant or a regular-file `.deft-directive-disable` kill-switch.

These residuals use dest forms that **#3354's generic `-o` / `--output` / `--outfile` harvest does not cover** (`cmake -E copy` positional dest, `script -q`, `gallery-dl -d`, `megadl --path`, `ncftpget`, `git apply --directory=…`, VCS checkout writers, and editor plant).

**Repo / tip:** `deftai/directive` @ `0c382e91d27308ad374de86092c184e12e4228c9`  
**Primary code:** `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts`  
**Attacker model:** Agent under **active UAT** with PreToolUse Shell hooks

**Already denied after #3354 (do not re-report):** `nc` / `netcat` / `7zz` / `msgfmt` / `msgcat` / `lz4` / `lzop` / `unrar` / `rar` / `aunpack` / `atool` / `ftpget` / `tftp` / `sqlite3` / `crane` / `objcopy` plus dest-flag `-o` / `--output` / `--outfile` on unknown write-shaped bins. Contrast: `curl -o` / `nc -o` remain settings-denied.

items.title: UAT residual dest forms deny authz and kill-switch writes

narrative.Acceptance: Given active UAT, when listed residual bins (cmake -E copy, script -q, gallery-dl -d, megadl --path, ncftpget, git apply --directory, svn export / fossil open peers, ed / nvim / nano) write into .deft/authz or plant .deft-directive-disable / .no-deft-directive, they classify as settings deny. Dest parsing covers those positional and flag dest forms. Unclassifiable write-shaped Shell under UAT is fail-closed, not silent allow.

items.title: Regressions versus already-denied peers and no false deny

narrative.Acceptance: Given the residual dest-form fix, when Vitest runs authz classify / decideHook regressions, curl -o and nc -o remain settings-denied and ordinary non-authz dests such as /tmp stay unclassifiable or allowed outside UAT write paths.
Given the security fix lands, when CHANGELOG [Unreleased] is read, it has a brief security note for #3382 with no exploit cookbook.
